speaker: Doctor
text: Since your inflammatory markers and uric acid are normal, does the pain worsen with activity or occur after a period of rest? REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_X-Ray

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Oligoarticular type). The age of onset, monoarticular presentation, normal inflammatory markers initially, and strong family history of similar issues are classic for this condition. I recommend checking ANA (Antinuclear Antibody) to assess for systemic risk.
